purpose: Non-reported, process-scoped CPU sampling for PERF-03; not part of published latency statistics.

identity.harness_delta: Only the main repetition count changed from 7 to 30000; one_run() and its T-S01 validation body are unchanged.

build.symbol_resolution: xperf resolved target executable functions from the colocated matching PDB; no source line-level DWARF/PDB line report was used.

workload.per_repetition_work: The unchanged one_run() body constructs/resolves the T-S01 problem, prepares registered Strategy B and HiGHS LP/convex providers, executes StrategyPort, verifies the registered complete optimal family and trajectory anchor, and checks the literal canonical H-relation/membership points.

profiled.command: VSDiagnostics session 89 -> attach PID 23164 -> run same executable -> stop session

paired_execution.assessment: Inconclusive. This is one sequential unprofiled/profiled pair under a changing, busy host. The profiled median is lower but the distributions overlap substantially; no profiler-overhead ratio, speedup, or latency difference is claimed.

profiler.mode: Process-scoped sampled CPU stacks; collector started before target launch and attached only to PID 23164.
profiler.privilege: No SeSystemProfilePrivilege; process-scoped sampling succeeded. WPR was not used in this capture.

trace.raw_etl_and_stack_html: Retained locally; not committed. Hashes above identify the exact local artifacts.

host.trace_load_observation: xperf per-logical-CPU utilization over 34 intervals (33.79 s): mean 12.45%, range 0.03–69.32%; includes the target plus unrelated background work.
host.load_context: Host was concurrently running other compiler/build and desktop processes; system utilization is retained as trace context, not normalized away.

conclusion: This single-process profile provides source-resolved evidence that sampled CPU work during the repeated, individually timed T-S01 one_run() operation is concentrated in the public StrategyPort -> Strategy B DirectJointWorkspace -> convex HiGHS QP path. It supports identifying that path as the sampled CPU hotspot for this exact diagnostic workload. It does not quantify exact unprofiled single-call latency attribution, generalize beyond T-S01, or support speedup, comparison, application-scale, or scalability claims. Independent review is still required for issue closure.
limitations: One profiled and one unprofiled execution only; order was unprofiled then profiled, not alternated.
The one_run() body is unchanged, but the diagnostic harness repetition count is increased to 30,000 to obtain usable in-process samples.
PDB-enabled Release semantics were retained, but this is not the exact no-PDB published binary.
Per-call timings include synchronous microsecond-scale operations; median and range vary substantially, and the paired wall-time difference is inconclusive.
Windows host utilization includes background work.
